name: io.github.ashlrai/phantom-secrets-mcp
title: Phantom Secrets
description: Value-blind secret metadata and gated workflows for AI coding agents through Phantom's local proxy.

tools.name: phantom_add_secret
tools.description: Deprecated unsafe plaintext secret entry. This tool refuses values because MCP arguments enter agent context. Use phantom_add_secret_interactive instead (no approval needed). Retained for compatibility: still requires `confirm: true` plus a one-use out-of-band `approval_token` (the operator enables effects with PHANTOM_MCP_EFFECTS=trusted-terminal; a call without the token prints a nonce on the server's stderr for `phantom mcp-approve <NONCE>` in a trusted terminal), and never stores anything.

approval_token.description:
Out-of-band approval token from `phantom mcp-approve <NONCE>`.
Format: "<nonce_hex>:<approval_token_hex>".

confirm.description:
Required. Must be true — the calling agent must confirm with the user
before invoking this tool. Defends against prompt-injected instructions
in project content (READMEs, issue comments, dependency docs) silently
mutating the vault.

tools.name: phantom_add_secret_interactive
tools.description: Safely add a secret by name without passing its value through MCP. Effect-free: it never accepts or echoes a value and touches no vault, file, or network, so it needs no approval and works with PHANTOM_MCP_EFFECTS unset. Returns `phantom add NAME`; the user runs it in a trusted terminal and types the value only at that terminal prompt, outside agent context.

confirm.description:
Optional, accepted for compatibility. This tool performs no effect: it
only returns the `phantom add NAME` command for the user to run in a
trusted terminal, so it needs neither confirmation nor approval. Legacy
approval fields from older callers are accepted and ignored.

name.description:
Name of the secret to add (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY). Must match
`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`. Never pass the secret value.

tools.name: phantom_apply_expiry_policy
tools.description: Scan the vault, apply read-only demotion to secrets whose TTL has expired, and (optionally) re-promote secrets that were demoted but have since been rotated. This blocks future vault retrieval and new `phantom exec`/foreground `phantom start` mapped-secret preflight; it does not recall values already injected or cached. Returns: { demoted: [{ name, expires_at, secs_overdue }], promoted: [{ name }], skipped_count, total_scanned }. Requires confirm:true plus a one-use out-of-band `approval_token` (the operator enables effects with PHANTOM_MCP_EFFECTS=trusted-terminal; a call without the token prints a nonce on the server's stderr for `phantom mcp-approve <NONCE>` in a trusted terminal) because it writes vault metadata.

also_promote_rotated.description:
When `true`, also promote secrets that were previously demoted but have
since been rotated (vault_mode ReadOnly → ReadWrite if `rotated_at` is
more recent than `expires_at`).  Default: `true`.

tools.name: phantom_audit_alerts
tools.description: Retrieve persisted leak-incident alert records from ~/.phantom/leak-alerts.jsonl. Each alert represents a high-confidence proxy response leak that was dispatched to configured backends (webhook/Slack/PagerDuty). Set 'backfill: true' to re-run correlation, persist new incidents/alerts, and dispatch configured notifications before returning the list; this requires confirm plus approval_token. Returns the most recent 'last' alerts (default 50, max 10000) in chronological order within a 1 MiB response, including: secret_name, location_label, confidence, event_count, alerted_at, backends_notified, and remediation advice. records_total counts every alert in the file, records_returned the alerts listed, and records_truncated is true when older ones were left out; max_records is the effective 'last'. For more run `phantom audit alerts --last N --json` in a terminal. Never exposes secret values. Read-only when backfill=false. Safe for AI agents.

backfill.description:
If true, re-run the leak correlation engine and emit pending alerts
before returning the list. Default: false.

confirm.description:
Required when `backfill=true` because correlation state and alert
records may be persisted and notification backends may be called.

last.description: Maximum number of recent alerts to return (default: 50).

tools.name: phantom_audit_analytics
tools.description: Export full audit analytics for compliance dashboards. Returns per-secret SecretAnalytics (access_count, daily_avg, max_daily, min_daily, anomaly_score) plus timestamped AccessRecords for the requested window. Supports JSON or CSV format. Use min_anomaly_score to filter to flagged secrets only (clamped to 0.0-1.0; NaN is refused). Never exposes secret values. Feed the output to Datadog, Grafana, CloudWatch, or any BI tool. window_days=0 returns all history; default is 30 days. format="csv" produces RFC 4180 CSV; format="json" produces structured JSON with 'analytics' (SecretAnalytics[]) and 'records' (AccessRecord[]) arrays. Records are bounded: only the newest max_records (default 1000, max 10000) are returned, within a 1 MiB response. records_total counts every matching record in the window and records_truncated is true when older ones were left out; analytics and time_series always cover the whole window. CSV carries the same counts in structuredContent and a second JSON text block. For a complete export run `phantom audit analytics --export FILE` in a terminal.

format.description:
Output format: "json" (default) or "csv", case-insensitive. Other
values are rejected with an invalid-params error.

max_records.description:
Maximum access records to return, newest kept (default: 1000; values
above 10000 are treated as 10000). A 1 MiB response ceiling may return
fewer; records_truncated and records_total then say so.

min_anomaly_score.description:
Only include secrets whose anomaly score is at or above this threshold
(range 0.0–1.0; other values are clamped into it). Omit to return all
secrets.

window_days.description:
Time window in days (default: 30): exactly the last N days of events.
0 means all available history.

tools.name: phantom_audit_anomalies
tools.description: Query the audit log for suspicious access patterns. Returns a findings array where each entry has: name (secret name), anomaly_type (spike | dormant | first_access), anomaly_score (0.0–1.0), access_count, last_access (ISO-8601), daily_avg, and context (human-readable explanation). Secret VALUES are never returned. Read-only; no confirm required. Anomaly types: 'spike' = single day >3x daily average; 'dormant' = access after >=7 consecutive quiet days. Use min_score to filter (default 0.4). Use period to limit the window. findings holds the highest-scoring max_records (default 1000, max 10000) within a 1 MiB response: total_findings counts every match, findings_returned the listed ones, and records_truncated is true when some were left out.

max_records.description:
Maximum findings to return, highest scores kept (default: 1000;
values above 10000 are treated as 10000). A 1 MiB response ceiling
may return fewer; total_findings stays exact and records_truncated
then says so.

min_score.description:
Minimum anomaly score to include (0.0–1.0; other values are clamped
into it). Defaults to 0.4.

period.description: Time period to analyse: "7d", "30d", or "all". Defaults to "30d".

tools.name: phantom_audit_anomalies_realtime
tools.description: Check whether a secret (or all secrets) has been accessed unusually based on windowed rate and quiet-period analysis of the current audit log. Unlike phantom_audit_anomalies (which uses multi-day daily-bucket statistics), this tool evaluates: (1) accesses within the last rolling hour vs max_accesses_per_hour threshold; (2) re-access after a quiet period longer than max_consecutive_quiet_days. Returns a findings array with fields: name, anomaly_score (0.0–1.0), alert (bool), reason (string), accesses_last_hour, max_quiet_gap_days. Secret VALUES are never returned. Read-only; no confirm required. Use threshold (default 0.5) to filter results. Pass name to check a single secret. Per-secret overrides from .phantom.toml [phantom.secrets.{name}.audit] are respected when max_accesses_per_hour / max_consecutive_quiet_days are omitted. findings holds the highest-scoring max_records (default 1000, max 10000) within a 1 MiB response: total_findings counts every match, findings_returned the listed ones, and records_truncated is true when some were left out.

max_accesses_per_hour.description:
Override: max accesses allowed within any rolling 1-hour window before
flagging a rate spike. Defaults to 100.

max_consecutive_quiet_days.description:
Override: number of consecutive quiet days after which a re-access
triggers a quiet-period alert. Defaults to 7.

max_records.description:
Maximum findings to return, highest scores kept (default: 1000;
values above 10000 are treated as 10000). A 1 MiB response ceiling
may return fewer; total_findings stays exact and records_truncated
then says so.

name.description: Filter to a single secret name. Omit to check all secrets.

threshold.description:
Minimum anomaly score (0.0–1.0; other values are clamped into it) to
include in results. Defaults to 0.5.

tools.name: phantom_audit_export_report
tools.description: Export audit log data or generate a structured compliance report. Two actions: 'export' — return raw audit rows (timestamp, datetime, operation, secret_name, pid, hostname, severity) filtered by date range, secret name, or operation type, in CSV or JSON format. Export rows are bounded: only the newest max_records (default 1000, max 10000) are returned, within a 1 MiB response; the first text block is the CSV or JSON array (header-only CSV or [] when nothing matches) and structuredContent plus a second JSON text block carry records_total, records_returned, records_truncated and max_records. For a complete export run `phantom audit export-range` in a terminal; 'report' — generate a full compliance report containing: (a) access-frequency heatmap per secret per calendar day, (b) leak-incident timeline with incident_id/secret_name/occurrences, (c) rotation-timing audit showing days since last vault.store per secret, (d) anomaly executive summary of high-score secrets. The returned report is bounded the same way: each of heatmap (most-accessed secrets), leak_timeline (newest incidents), rotation_audit (longest since rotation) and anomaly_summary (highest scores) holds at most max_records entries, within a 1 MiB response; total_events, distinct_secrets and high_severity_events stay exact, <list>_total and <list>_returned count each list, and records_truncated is true when any entry was left out. Use 'from'/'to' (YYYY-MM-DD) to scope the date range. Set 'save: true' to persist the complete report to ~/.phantom/reports/; saving requires confirm plus approval_token. Never exposes secret values. Read-only (save=false). Safe for AI agents.

action.description:
Action: "export" to get raw rows as CSV/JSON, or "report" to get a
full compliance report. Default: "report".

confirm.description: Required when `save=true` because a report is persisted to disk.

format.description:
Output format: "csv" or "json", case-insensitive. Default: "json".
Other values are rejected with an invalid-params error.

from.description: Start date inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD). Omit for no lower bound.

max_records.description:
Maximum audit rows `action="export"` returns, newest kept, and
maximum entries in each list of the returned `action="report"`
(default: 1000; values above 10000 are treated as 10000). A 1 MiB
response ceiling may return fewer; records_truncated and the totals
then say so. A saved report is always complete.

operation.description: Filter rows to operations containing this string. Omit for all ops.

save.description: Save the compliance report to ~/.phantom/reports/ (report action only).

secret_name.description: Filter rows to this secret name only (exact match). Omit for all secrets.

to.description: End date inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD). Omit for no upper bound.

tools.name: phantom_audit_hotspot_alerts
tools.description: Inspect per-secret access-velocity spike alerts without manually parsing the audit log. Returns alerts for secrets whose access count in the rolling 24-hour window either (a) exceeds 5× the 7-day mean baseline, or (b) includes a burst of ≥100 accesses within any 5-minute window. Each alert record contains: secret_name, current_velocity (24h count), baseline_velocity (7-day daily mean), alert_level (always 'high'), first_spike_ts (ISO-8601), ack_status ('unacked'|'acked'|'snoozed'), peak_5m_count, and trigger (human-readable description). Secret VALUES are never returned. Set ack=true to acknowledge all returned alerts (removes them from the active list). Set snooze_seconds>0 with ack=true to snooze instead of fully acknowledging. Pass include_acked=true to also return already-acknowledged or snoozed alerts. Use secret_name to filter to a specific secret. Read-only when ack=false; ack=true persists acknowledgement state and requires confirm plus approval_token. alerts lists at most 10000 (unacked first, then fastest) within a 1 MiB response: total_alerts counts every match, alerts_returned the listed ones, and records_truncated is true when some were left out; ack=true acknowledges every matching alert, listed or not.

ack.description:
If true, acknowledge (clear) all returned unacked alerts.
Default: false (read-only inspection).

confirm.description: Required when `ack=true` because acknowledgement state is persisted.

include_acked.description:
Include already-acknowledged or snoozed alerts in the response.
Default: false (only unacked alerts).

secret_name.description: If set, only return alerts for this specific secret name.

snooze_seconds.description:
If > 0 and `ack` is true, snooze the alert for this many seconds instead
of fully acknowledging it. Default: 0 (full ack when `ack` is true).

tools.name: phantom_audit_incidents
tools.description: Return active leak incidents derived from proxy.response_leak audit events. Incidents are correlated by (secret_name, location) within a 24-hour window. min_confidence (default 0.7) filters by confidence score: 0.5 = single leak event; 0.95 = same secret leaked >3 times within 1 hour. Each incident includes: incident_id, secret_name (never the value), location_label, first_seen_ts, last_seen_ts, event_count, confidence, remediation. Incidents whose secret was subsequently stored are omitted. incidents lists the persisted incident store. The proxy only appends audit events, so leak events from the last 24 h that no backfill has persisted yet are correlated in memory and listed separately in uncorrelated_incidents (uncorrelated_count), with a next_step; treat them as possible leaks. Always returns JSON {incident_count, min_confidence, incidents, uncorrelated_count, uncorrelated_incidents, audit_log_present, next_step} (also as structuredContent). Each list holds at most max_records (default 1000, max 10000), most confident first, within a 1 MiB response: incident_count and uncorrelated_count stay exact, incidents_returned and uncorrelated_incidents_returned count the listed entries, and records_truncated is true when some were left out. Read-only: it never writes incident or alert state.

max_records.description:
Maximum entries in each of incidents and uncorrelated_incidents,
most confident kept (default: 1000; values above 10000 are treated as
10000). A 1 MiB response ceiling may return fewer; incident_count and
uncorrelated_count stay exact and records_truncated then says so.

min_confidence.description:
Only return incidents whose confidence score is at or above this value
(range 0.0–1.0). Defaults to 0.7.

tools.name: phantom_audit_recent
tools.description: List the last N audit events from the HMAC-chained audit log. Returns structured JSONL — each line is a JSON object with fields: seq, ts (Unix epoch), op (operation name), name (secret name, if applicable), pid, process. Secret VALUES are never recorded in the audit log and will never appear here. Supports optional filtering by op prefix or exact secret name. Reads only the newest 8 MiB of the log: `window_truncated: true` means older events were not examined, so `matched_in_window` is not a total and `total_in_log` is omitted. `unparsable_lines` counts lines in the window that are not audit events and were skipped (run `phantom audit verify` to check the chain). Read-only; no confirm required. Requires PHANTOM_AUDIT=1 to have been set when operations were performed.

n.description: Maximum number of recent audit events to return (default: 20, max: 200).

name_filter.description: Filter by secret name (exact match). Omit for all secrets.

op_filter.description: Filter by operation name prefix (e.g. "vault.retrieve", "cloud"). Omit for all ops.

tools.name: phantom_audit_stats
tools.description: Aggregate access counts, last-access timestamps, daily averages, and anomaly scores from the HMAC-chained audit log. Returns JSON only — never exposes secret values. Anomaly detection flags: (1) any single day with >3× the daily average access count (score 0.6); (2) first access after ≥7 days of inactivity (score 0.5). Use period to limit the window ("7d", "30d", "all"). Use min_anomaly_score to filter to flagged secrets only (e.g. 0.5). Requires PHANTOM_AUDIT=1 to have been set when secrets were accessed.

min_anomaly_score.description:
Only include secrets whose anomaly score is at or above this threshold
(range 0.0–1.0; other values are clamped into it). Omit or set to 0.0
to return all secrets.

period.description: Time period to analyse: "7d", "30d", or "all". Defaults to "all".

tools.name: phantom_capability
tools.description: Return a value-free capability card for the small conversation-native facade: allowed local verbs, requestable verbs, place/seal state, expiry, and facade hard denials. This is not a policy oracle for the advanced compatibility catalog, whose mutating tools retain separate legacy confirm plus out-of-band local approval gates and are not Locus-sealed.

tools.name: phantom_check
tools.description: Check for security issues. With runtime=true, scans every environment variable of this server for a phantom token (leak detection). A variable is excused only when PHANTOM_PROXY_PORT and PHANTOM_PROXY_TOKEN lead to a live Phantom proxy (its health endpoint answers) and the session lists the variable in PHANTOM_SESSION_KEYS; excused names are reported in `excused` and `proxy_session` is true. Session variables with no live proxy are reported in `session_warning` and excuse nothing. Otherwise, scans the same dotenv files as `phantom check` for unprotected real secrets: .env, .env.local, .env.development, .env.development.local, .env.production, .env.production.local, .env.test, .env.test.local, plus the configured dotenv_path; a symlink is not followed and makes the result indeterminate. Returns a human summary plus a value-blind JSON report (also as structuredContent) shaped like `phantom check --json`: {mode, clean, findings: [{kind, path?, name?}], warnings, indeterminate?, proxy_session?, excused?, session_warning?}. Reports names and paths only, never values or phantom tokens.

runtime.description: Check if phantom tokens are in environment without proxy running

tools.name: phantom_cloud_pull
tools.description: Pull and decrypt a personal-vault snapshot from a separately commissioned Phantom Cloud deployment and entitled account; the public hosted service is not currently commissioned for authenticated use. DESTRUCTIVE — writes local vault entries; force=true declares overwrites but never bypasses approval. With force=false, existing entries are skipped; any partial result preserves the prior merge base, records a durable reconciliation requirement, and blocks cloud push until a fully reconciled pull. Requires `confirm: true` plus an out-of-band `approval_token`.

force.description:
Declare overwrite of existing local secrets (default: false). This does
not bypass confirmation or out-of-band approval. With false, skipped
entries retain the prior merge base and block push until reconciliation.

tools.name: phantom_cloud_push
tools.description: Push a client-encrypted local vault to a separately commissioned Phantom Cloud deployment and entitled account; the public hosted service is not currently commissioned for authenticated use. The configured service receives ciphertext rather than decrypted vault values. Requires phantom login first. DESTRUCTIVE — overwrites the existing cloud copy; damage from a prompt-injected push propagates to every machine that later pulls. Requires `confirm: true` plus a one-use out-of-band `approval_token` (the operator enables effects with PHANTOM_MCP_EFFECTS=trusted-terminal; a call without the token prints a nonce on the server's stderr for `phantom mcp-approve <NONCE>` in a trusted terminal); the agent must ask the user for explicit consent before calling.

confirm.description:
Required. Must be true — the calling agent must confirm with the user
before invoking this tool. A push overwrites the cloud copy of the
project's vault; damage from a prompt-injected push propagates to every
machine that later pulls.

tools.name: phantom_cloud_status
tools.description: Check authentication status, plan, and last sync version against a separately commissioned Phantom Cloud deployment; the public hosted service is not currently commissioned for authenticated use. This uses the stored cloud credential and makes a provider request; requires confirm plus approval_token.

confirm.description: Required. Must be true before the provider or persistent-state effect.

tools.name: phantom_compliance_status
tools.description: Return the compliance state of the current Phantom project as a structured JSON badge. Checks: vault_accessible (every secret of this project can be read here; false for an encrypted-file vault this process cannot open, even when the OS keychain holds some entries, the same rule as `phantom agent doctor`), audit_enabled (PHANTOM_AUDIT env var is set), precommit_installed (git pre-commit hook contains the current local-only phantom check), env_clean (no unprotected real secrets in any dotenv phantom check scans: .env, .env.local, .env.development, .env.development.local, .env.production, .env.production.local, .env.test, .env.test.local and the configured dotenv_path; read without opening the vault, so it is reported before init and with a locked vault), secrets_have_ttl (every vault secret has an expiry (expires_at) or a rotation policy set; false when not every secret can be read; the detail gives the exact count and names at most 20). Each check is true/false with an optional detail string. Overall 'compliant' is true only when all checks pass. Read-only.

tools.name: phantom_copy_secret
tools.description: Copy a secret into a distinct initialized target through one exact-before target transaction. Refuses existing target vault, lifecycle-config, or managed-dotenv ownership; never overwrites. On success it creates both the target vault entry and managed-dotenv phantom mapping, with dotenv committed last. This is an exfiltration-capable cross-project write and requires confirm plus an out-of-band approval token before any source value retrieval.

confirm.description:
Required. Must be true — the calling agent must confirm with the user
before invoking this tool. Copying writes secrets into another vault,
which an attacker can use as an exfiltration primitive.

name.description: Name of the secret to copy from the current project

rename.description:
Optional new name for the secret in the target project. Copy refuses
if the target vault, lifecycle config, or managed dotenv already owns
this name; there is no overwrite mode.

target_dir.description:
Path to the target project directory (must be phantom-initialized).
`..` segments are rejected to prevent prompt-injected target-dir
obfuscation; pass the full destination path explicitly.

tools.name: phantom_do
tools.description: Conversation-native engineering action planning. phase=propose (default) accepts only Phantom's closed Cargo action schema and returns a value-free canonical digest, effect classification, local workspace fingerprint, and exact activation blockers without executing anything. phase=execute is reserved and always hard denied until verified Locus authority, rollback-resistant replay, trusted handles, OS confinement, and correlated evidence are active. There are no bearer or secret-value fields; bounded action selectors are never treated as authority and are never echoed.

oneOf.description: Canonicalize and report one exact closed action without executing it.
Reserved for the future sealed runtime. Currently always denied.

action.description: One closed Cargo engineering action. Arbitrary shell commands are not representable.

tools.name: phantom_doctor
tools.description: Run repository-local Phantom health checks: config validity, .env protection, .gitignore, .env.example, and pre-commit hook. This tool does not open or provision a vault. Set fix=true to apply reviewed repository-local repairs; fix=true requires `confirm: true` plus a one-use out-of-band `approval_token` (the operator enables effects with PHANTOM_MCP_EFFECTS=trusted-terminal; a call without the token prints a nonce on the server's stderr for `phantom mcp-approve <NONCE>` in a trusted terminal), while fix=false is read-only and ungated. Returns a human summary plus a value-blind JSON report (also as structuredContent) in the `phantom doctor --json` shape: {ok, issues, fixed, checks: [{status, message, fix?, fixed?}], mcp_clients}. `fix` is the hint for that check only; with fix=true a repaired check keeps its warn status and gains `fixed`. Check messages and hints are this tool's own and differ from the CLI's; mcp_clients is always [] because this tool does not inspect global client configs.

approval_token.description:
Out-of-band approval token from `phantom mcp-approve <NONCE>`. Only
required when fix=true (read-only doctor runs do not need approval).

confirm.description: Required when fix=true because files may be created or modified.

fix.description: Auto-fix safe issues (install hooks, generate .env.example, etc.)

tools.name: phantom_env
tools.description: Generate a .env.example file from .env. Secrets are replaced with descriptive placeholders; non-secret config values are preserved. Safe to commit to version control. Writes a file: requires `confirm: true` plus a one-use out-of-band `approval_token` (the operator enables effects with PHANTOM_MCP_EFFECTS=trusted-terminal; a call without the token prints a nonce on the server's stderr for `phantom mcp-approve <NONCE>` in a trusted terminal).

confirm.description: Required. Must be true because this writes an env example file.

tools.name: phantom_expiry_enforce
tools.description: Check the vault's TTL metadata (set with `phantom expiry set`) for expired secrets and return a structured list, the same answer as `phantom expiry enforce --json`. Each entry has: name (string), expires_at (Unix u64), secs_overdue (u64), status (human-readable string). `expired` holds only secrets whose expiry has passed. With fail_closed=true, secrets that have no expiry set are violations too and are named in no_expiry_policy (status='no_expiry_policy'); it is empty otherwise. Returns { expired: [...], no_expiry_policy: [...], ok_count, no_expiry_count, fail_closed, pass }. pass=true means no action is needed. Read-only; no confirm required. Secret VALUES are never returned.

fail_closed.description:
If true, also treat secrets with no expiry policy as violations.
Defaults to false (permissive: only hard-expired secrets are reported).

tools.name: phantom_init
tools.description: Initialize Phantom through one exact-before project transaction: read a safe project-local dotenv, compare-and-swap every vault entry, persist config, and rewrite the dotenv with phantom tokens last. Concurrent file or vault changes abort and transaction-owned writes are rolled back where verifiable. Requires confirm plus out-of-band approval.

approval_token.description:
Out-of-band approval token from `phantom mcp-approve <NONCE>`.
Format: "<nonce_hex>:<approval_token_hex>".

confirm.description: Required. Must be true because init stores secrets and rewrites .env.

env_path.description: Path to the .env file (defaults to .env in current directory)

tools.name: phantom_leak_incidents_realtime
tools.description: Query active leak incidents for a real-time security dashboard. Returns incidents with confidence > 0.5 seen within the last 24 hours, sorted by confidence descending. Each entry contains: secret_name (never the value), location_label, confidence, first_seen (ISO-8601), last_seen (ISO-8601), incident_id. Set min_confidence (default 0.5) to narrow results. incidents lists persisted incidents; leak events from the last 24 h that no backfill has persisted yet are correlated in memory and listed in uncorrelated_incidents (uncorrelated_count, same entry shape) with a next_step. Always returns JSON {incident_count, min_confidence, effect, rotation_performed, incidents, uncorrelated_count, uncorrelated_incidents, audit_log_present, next_step}. Each list holds at most max_records (default 1000, max 10000), most confident first, within a 1 MiB response: incident_count and uncorrelated_count stay exact, incidents_returned and uncorrelated_incidents_returned count the listed entries, and records_truncated is true when some were left out. Never rotates, writes incident or alert state, or exposes secret values. Use a separately approved rotation tool to remediate.

max_records.description:
Maximum entries in each of incidents and uncorrelated_incidents,
most confident kept (default: 1000; values above 10000 are treated as
10000). A 1 MiB response ceiling may return fewer; incident_count and
uncorrelated_count stay exact and records_truncated then says so.

min_confidence.description:
Only return incidents whose confidence score is at or above this value
(range 0.0–1.0). Defaults to 0.5 per spec (active incident threshold).

tools.name: phantom_list_secrets
tools.description: List all secret names in the Phantom vault. Returns names only — never exposes actual secret values. Use this to see what secrets are configured. Returns a summary plus JSON {count, secrets: [{name, service}]} (also as structuredContent). Before `phantom init` it opens no vault and returns {count: 0, secrets: [], initialized: false, next_step} instead of an error.

tools.name: phantom_list_with_expiry
tools.description: List all secret names with their TTL/expiry status. Shows days remaining, EXPIRED flag, or 'no expiry' for each secret. Never returns secret values. Use it to audit which credentials need an explicit provider rotation or local expiry-policy review. Returns a summary plus JSON {count, show_expiry, expired, expiring_soon, secrets: [{name, service, status?, expires_at?, days_remaining?}]} (also as structuredContent). Before `phantom init` it opens no vault and returns an empty report with initialized: false and next_step instead of an error.

show_expiry.description: Include TTL/expiry status for each secret (countdown, expired flag, etc.)

tools.name: phantom_remove_secret
tools.description: Transactionally remove a secret's vault value, lifecycle configuration, and exact managed-dotenv mapping. DESTRUCTIVE — a successful removal is recoverable only from a separately retained backup. Uses exact before-images and rolls back only transaction-owned changes. Requires `confirm: true` plus an out-of-band `approval_token`; review the exact value-blind effect before approval.

confirm.description:
Required. Must be true — the calling agent must confirm with the user
before invoking this tool. Defends against prompt-injected instructions
deleting secrets.

name.description: Name of the secret to remove

tools.name: phantom_rotate
tools.description: Regenerate all phantom tokens in .env. Old tokens become invalid — any running `phantom exec` / dev server that cached them will break until it picks up the new .env. Real secrets in the vault are unchanged. DESTRUCTIVE; requires `confirm: true` plus a one-use out-of-band `approval_token` (the operator enables effects with PHANTOM_MCP_EFFECTS=trusted-terminal; a call without the token prints a nonce on the server's stderr for `phantom mcp-approve <NONCE>` in a trusted terminal); the agent must ask the user for explicit consent before calling.

confirm.description:
Required. Must be true — the calling agent must confirm with the user
before invoking this tool. Rotating invalidates every live phantom token
and will break any process that cached the old tokens (e.g. a running
`phantom exec` or dev server) until it picks up the new .env.

tools.name: phantom_rotate_promote
tools.description: DEPRECATED hard denial: legacy candidates were local phm_cand_ placeholders, not provider-issued credentials. This tool never validates, promotes, or changes a vault value and ignores compatibility parameters, including approval_token: no approval can activate it. Live provider issuance is also hard-denied until compensated recovery exists; rotate at the provider and store the replacement interactively.

approval_token.description: Ignored compatibility field. No approval can enable this tool.

confirm.description: Ignored compatibility field. The tool is always denied.

name.description: Ignored compatibility field. No candidate is promoted.

tools.name: phantom_rotate_provider
tools.description: Provider-rotation compatibility boundary. Shipped builds hard-deny automated live provider issuance before credential access or network I/O because the provider contract does not yet preserve a durable value-free recovery handle and verified abort path for local persistence failure. Unit-test mock providers are not production capability evidence. Current calls return a value-blind hard denial without consuming an approval or opening the vault. The confirm and approval fields are reserved for a future effectful, compensated implementation.

approval_token.description:
Out-of-band approval token from `phantom mcp-approve <NONCE>`.
Format: `"<nonce_hex>:<approval_token_hex>"`.

confirm.description:
Required. Must be `true` — the calling agent must confirm with the
user before rotating a live credential. Vendor rotation calls
external APIs and permanently invalidates the current key.

name.description: Name of the secret to rotate (e.g. `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`).

provider.description:
Which provider to use: `"stripe"`, `"github"`, `"aws"`, `"google"`,
or `"vercel"`. When set, it must match the `provider` field in the
secret's `[phantom.secrets.{name}.rotation_provider]` config block.
Optional — when omitted, the provider is resolved from that config
block in `.phantom.toml`.

tools.name: phantom_rotate_with_candidate
tools.description: DEPRECATED hard denial: legacy shadow rotation generated only a local phm_cand_ placeholder, not a provider-issued credential. This tool never creates or stores a candidate and ignores compatibility parameters, including approval_token: no approval can activate it. Live provider issuance is also hard-denied until compensated recovery exists; rotate at the provider and store the replacement interactively.

approval_token.description: Ignored compatibility field. No approval can enable this tool.

auto_promote_ttl_secs.description: Ignored compatibility field. No candidate TTL is created.

confirm.description: Ignored compatibility field. The tool is always denied.

name.description: Ignored compatibility field. No candidate is created.

tools.name: phantom_rotate_with_expiry
tools.description: DEPRECATED compatibility name: atomically remap all local phm_ placeholders. The legacy days_ttl field is validated but no longer renews `rotated_at`, `expires_at`, or rotation_policy because no provider credential changes. Provider credentials and incident state remain unchanged. MUTATING — invalidates current Phantom placeholders; requires confirm:true plus an out-of-band approval_token.

confirm.description:
Required. Must be true — the calling agent must confirm with the user
before remapping all local Phantom tokens (invalidating cached
placeholders). Provider credentials and expiry metadata remain unchanged.

days_ttl.description:
Deprecated compatibility field. Must be greater than zero, but a local
Phantom token remap does not renew credential TTL or lifecycle metadata.

tools.name: phantom_rotation_schedule_next
tools.description: Return the next scheduled rotation time for a named secret. Reads the secret's effective RotationSchedule (per-secret override or global policy) and computes when rotation is next due. A per-secret `rotate_every` ("90d", "12w") is an exact interval: strategy "interval" with interval_days; an unparseable value is a config error. Returns: { name, strategy, interval_days (u64 or null), next_rotation_unix (u64 or null), next_rotation_iso (ISO-8601 or null), last_rotated_unix (u64 or null), last_rotated_iso (ISO-8601 or null), overdue (bool) }. Read-only; no confirm required. Secret VALUES are never returned.

name.description: Name of the secret to query (e.g. `OPENAI_API_KEY`).

tools.name: phantom_secret_rotation_due
tools.description: Query which secrets in the vault are due for rotation. Returns a JSON object with: due (list of secrets already expired), warning (list of secrets expiring within warn_days, default 7), ok (list of secrets with sufficient TTL remaining), no_ttl (list of secrets with neither an expiry nor a rotation policy). A secret with expires_at but no rotation policy is still classified by its expiry. Each entry has: name, status (expired|warning|ok|no_ttl), days_remaining (null if no expiry; negative means already expired), expires_at (ISO-8601 or null), has_rotation_policy (bool). Secret VALUES are never returned. Read-only; no confirm required.

warn_days.description: Warn when expiry is within this many days. Defaults to 7.

tools.name: phantom_secrets_auto_rotate
tools.description: DEPRECATED compatibility name: remap the local phm_ placeholder for one already-protected secret. This does not rotate or validate the provider credential, does not change `rotated_at` / `expires_at` / TTL policy, does not clear leak incidents, and cannot sync an unchanged credential (`sync: true` is rejected). When audit logging is enabled, success records `secret.token_remapped`. MUTATING — atomically rewrites .env and requires `confirm: true` plus an out-of-band approval token. Secret VALUES are never returned or logged.

confirm.description:
Required. Must be true — the calling agent must confirm with the user
before remapping the local Phantom token. This rewrites `.env` and can
disrupt running services that cached the old placeholder, but it does
not alter provider credentials or lifecycle metadata.

name.description:
Name of the already-protected secret whose local `phm_` placeholder
should be remapped. The provider credential is not rotated.

sync.description:
Deprecated compatibility field. `true` is rejected because token
remapping does not create a credential that can truthfully be synced.

tools.name: phantom_secrets_expiry_check
tools.description: Query the local vault for secrets that are expired or expiring soon. Returns a JSON array where each entry has: name (string), days_remaining (i64, floored — negative means already expired, so a secret that expired under 24 h ago reports -1), expires_at (Unix epoch u64), status (human-readable string), expired (bool). Use the `days` parameter (default 7) to tune the look-ahead window. Secrets with no TTL set are omitted — use phantom_secret_rotation_due to also surface those. Secret VALUES are never returned. Read-only; no confirm required.

days.description:
Warn about secrets expiring within this many days (default: 7).
Set to 0 to return only already-expired secrets.

tools.name: phantom_setup_workspace
tools.description: Conversation-native, value-blind workspace setup. phase=propose returns an exact sealed plan; if the machine-local plan-seal key is absent, provisioning it requires confirm plus approval_token. phase=request_apply always requires both gates because it persists a bearerless trusted-terminal request. phase=status is read-only. MCP never claims or applies workspace changes.

oneOf.description: Inspect and return the current value-blind sealed plan.
Create a bearerless request for trusted-terminal application.

confirm.description:
Required for phases that persist machine-local state (`propose` when the
plan-seal key has not been provisioned, and every `request_apply`).

plan_id.description: Exact plan digest returned by the latest propose phase.

pre_state_id.description: Exact keyed pre-state digest returned by the latest propose phase.

request_id.description: Bearerless request identifier returned by request_apply.

tools.name: phantom_status
tools.description: Read repository-local Phantom status without opening or provisioning a vault: project ID, managed dotenv protection counts, and configured service mappings. Vault backend and stored-secret inventory are deliberately not inspected; use phantom_list_secrets for the latter. Returns a summary plus JSON {initialized, project_id, vault_inspected, dotenv: {path, entries, phantom_tokens, unprotected} | null, services, next_step} (also as structuredContent).

tools.name: phantom_sync
tools.description: Show sync configuration and what secrets would be synced to deployment platforms (Vercel, Railway). This is an informational tool that never pushes: actual sync requires platform API tokens and `phantom sync` in a terminal. platform must be `vercel` or `railway` (case-insensitive); any other value is refused with invalid params before the vault is opened. Use it to understand and explain the sync setup. Returns a summary plus JSON {configured, platform_filter, configured_platforms, vault_secret_count, targets, next_step} (also as structuredContent).

platform.description: Platform to show: `vercel` or `railway` (case-insensitive). Omit it, or pass an empty string, to show every configured target. Any other value is refused.

project_id.description: Override project ID for this sync

tools.name: phantom_team_create
tools.description: Request a new team from a separately commissioned hosted Pro pilot and entitled account; the public hosted service and self-serve Pro billing are not currently commissioned. If accepted, the authenticated user becomes the owner. Mutating provider request: requires confirm:true plus an out-of-band approval_token.

confirm.description:
Required. Must be true — confirms the user wants to request a new team
from a separately commissioned hosted Pro pilot. This is not evidence
of current public entitlement or self-serve billing.

name.description: Name for the new team (human-readable label)

tools.name: phantom_team_invite
tools.description: Invite someone to a team by GitHub username. Requires a separately commissioned hosted service and entitled account; the public hosted service is not currently commissioned. The caller must be a team owner or admin; the hosted API permits assigning only member or admin (not owner). Mutating provider request: requires confirm:true plus an out-of-band approval_token.

confirm.description:
Required. Must be true — confirms the user wants to add this person
to the team. Defends against prompt-injected instructions silently
expanding team membership.

github_login.description: GitHub username of the user to invite (no @ prefix)

role.description:
Role to assign. Hosted invitations accept only `member` or `admin`;
ownership transfer is a separate lifecycle operation and is not exposed.

tools.name: phantom_team_key_publish
tools.description: One-time setup: register this device's public key with the team so you can send and receive encrypted vaults. Requires a separately commissioned hosted service and entitled account; the public hosted service is not currently commissioned. Must be called before phantom_team_vault_push or phantom_team_vault_pull. Idempotent — safe to call again after a key rotation. Mutating provider request: requires `confirm: true` plus a one-use out-of-band `approval_token` (the operator enables effects with PHANTOM_MCP_EFFECTS=trusted-terminal; a call without the token prints a nonce on the server's stderr for `phantom mcp-approve <NONCE>` in a trusted terminal).

confirm.description: Required for mutating operations that publish local key material.

tools.name: phantom_team_list
tools.description: List teams the authenticated user belongs to. Requires a separately commissioned hosted service and entitled account; the public hosted service is not currently commissioned. Returns team id, name, and role. Uses the stored cloud credential and makes a provider request; requires confirm plus approval_token.

confirm.description: Required. Must be true before the provider or persistent-state effect.

tools.name: phantom_team_members
tools.description: List members of a team by team_id. Requires a separately commissioned hosted service and entitled account; the public hosted service is not currently commissioned. Returns GitHub login, email, and role. Uses the stored cloud credential and makes a provider request; requires confirm plus approval_token.

confirm.description: Required for mutating operations that publish local key material.

tools.name: phantom_team_vault_pull
tools.description: Download and decrypt the team vault for this project into the local vault. Requires a separately commissioned hosted service and entitled account; the public hosted service is not currently commissioned. Use this (not phantom_cloud_pull) when secrets were shared by a teammate via phantom_team_vault_push. Overwrites local secrets: requires confirm:true plus a one-use out-of-band `approval_token` (the operator enables effects with PHANTOM_MCP_EFFECTS=trusted-terminal; a call without the token prints a nonce on the server's stderr for `phantom mcp-approve <NONCE>` in a trusted terminal).

confirm.description:
Required. Must be true — push/pull mutates the team's shared vault
(push) or overwrites local secrets with the team copy (pull). Both
are write operations that need user consent.

tools.name: phantom_team_vault_push
tools.description: Push this project's secrets to the shared team vault so all members can pull them. Requires a separately commissioned hosted service and entitled account; the public hosted service is not currently commissioned. Encrypts client-side for each member who has registered a key (phantom_team_key_publish). Mutating: requires confirm:true plus a one-use out-of-band `approval_token` (the operator enables effects with PHANTOM_MCP_EFFECTS=trusted-terminal; a call without the token prints a nonce on the server's stderr for `phantom mcp-approve <NONCE>` in a trusted terminal).

confirm.description:
Required. Must be true — push/pull mutates the team's shared vault
(push) or overwrites local secrets with the team copy (pull). Both
are write operations that need user consent.

tools.name: phantom_unwrap
tools.description: Reverse phantom_wrap: restore original package.json scripts from their `:raw` variants and remove the `:raw` entries. Writes package.json: requires `confirm: true` plus a one-use out-of-band `approval_token` (the operator enables effects with PHANTOM_MCP_EFFECTS=trusted-terminal; a call without the token prints a nonce on the server's stderr for `phantom mcp-approve <NONCE>` in a trusted terminal).

confirm.description: Required. Must be true because this modifies package.json.

tools.name: phantom_validate_all
tools.description: Run live credential health checks for all secrets in the vault. Each secret is validated against its target API (OpenAI, Stripe, GitHub, Anthropic, AWS, or a generic HTTP check). Returns a JSON compliance report with: total, valid, invalid, unreachable, not_checked counts and per-secret entries (name, validator, status, reason, checked_at). Secret VALUES are never returned or logged. This retrieves credentials, makes real outbound provider requests, and persists value-free validation metadata; it requires confirm plus approval_token and should run during a maintenance window.

confirm.description:
Required because validation retrieves credentials, calls provider APIs,
and persists the value-free result metadata.

jobs.description: Maximum number of concurrent validation jobs (default: 4, max: 16).

tools.name: phantom_validate_secret
tools.description: Query the last-known validation status for a specific secret. Returns: last_check_ts (Unix epoch, 0 = never checked), is_valid (bool), failure_reason (string or null), validator_name (which validator ran), and is_stale (whether the check is older than 24 h). If the stored results cannot be read, metadata_error is true, a note says why, and the other status fields are null rather than reporting never_checked. This tool reads persisted ValidationMetadata — it does NOT make a live HTTP request. Use phantom_validate_all to trigger a fresh check. Read-only; no confirm required. Secret VALUES are never returned.

name.description:
Name of the secret to query validation status for (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY).
Never the value — this tool only reads stored metadata.

tools.name: phantom_validation_history
tools.description: Retrieve the history of past automated validation runs. Each entry contains: started_at (Unix epoch), finished_at, total, pass, fail, unreachable, not_checked, and an optional error string. Use `limit` (default 20, max 100) to control how many recent entries are returned. Secret VALUES are never returned. Read-only; no confirm required.

limit.description: Maximum number of recent runs to return (default: 20, max: 100).

tools.name: phantom_validation_schedule
tools.description: Get or set the automated background validation schedule. Pass `interval` to update (accepted values: 'hourly', '6h', '12h', 'daily', 'daily@2am', 'weekly', 'disabled'). Omit `interval` to read the current schedule and staleness status. Returns schedule, last_run_at, and staleness indicators. Read-only when interval is omitted. Providing interval persists scheduler state and requires confirm plus approval_token.

confirm.description: Required when `interval` is present because scheduler state is persisted.

interval.description:
New schedule interval to set: "hourly", "6h", "daily", "daily@2am",
"weekly", "disabled". Omit to read the current schedule only.

tools.name: phantom_why
tools.description: Explain why an environment variable is or isn't protected by Phantom. classification is `protected` (has a phantom token), `secret_unprotected` (next_step says to run `phantom init`), `public_key` or `not_secret`, and is null when the key is not in the dotenv (found=false). reason names the heuristic: `phantom_token`, `key_name`, `connection_pattern`, `value_pattern`, `public_prefix_with_secret_value`, `public_prefix` or `no_secret_pattern`; matched_pattern is the matched key fragment or prefix. Value-blind: it reads .phantom.toml and the dotenv, never the vault, so it answers while the vault is locked and before `phantom init` (it then classifies ./.env, and exec is null). For a protected key it also says how `phantom exec` treats it. exec.delivery judges the key alone: `proxied` (a built-in route injects the real value for exec.upstream), `no_route` (the child gets only a session token that no provider accepts, so calls with it fail), `withheld` (exec never hands the child this provider-management or sync credential), `connection_string_refused` or `custom_route_refused` (exec will not start). exec.blocked_by is non-null when the config stops exec from starting for every key: {service, reason: `custom_route`, `altered_builtin_route` or `connection_string`, key}. next_step explains anything but an unblocked `proxied`. Returns a summary plus value-free JSON {key, dotenv_exists, found, classification, protected, reason, matched_pattern, service, exec: {delivery, service, upstream, blocked_by} | null, next_step} (also as structuredContent).

tools.name: phantom_wrap
tools.description: Wrap package.json scripts with the installed local `phantom exec --` command so secrets are injected via the proxy at runtime. Saves originals as `script:raw` variants. Uses a heuristic to pick dev/start/build/serve/deploy scripts and skip lint/test/format scripts. Writes package.json: requires `confirm: true` plus a one-use out-of-band `approval_token` (the operator enables effects with PHANTOM_MCP_EFFECTS=trusted-terminal; a call without the token prints a nonce on the server's stderr for `phantom mcp-approve <NONCE>` in a trusted terminal).

confirm.description: Required. Must be true because this modifies package.json.

only.description: Only wrap specific scripts (by name). If empty, uses default heuristic.
